pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_events/libs/__tests__/eventSourceRegistry.test.ts:45 The context's source-reading guard counts only literal `source_type: "x"` assignments and silently skips every other form, so `source_type: DRIVE_SOURCE_TYPE.to_string()` (src-tauri/src/commands/drive/mod.rs:138) and `source_type: tpl.source.to_string()` (src-tauri/src/commands/communication/events.rs:349) are invisible to it. Their tokens (local_drive, the mock_seed sources) are covered today only because someone registered them by hand, so this is a blind spot, not a live leak.

techniques.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_events/libs/__tests__/eventSourceRegistry.test.ts:45 The matcher has no rule that refuses a non-literal source_type assignment, so a constant, field or format! form passes as if it complied. The repo owns the scanned tree, so the precondition holds.
src/features/overview/sub_events/libs/__tests__/eventSourceRegistry.test.ts:65 The walked population has a floor, so a moved crate or a broken walk goes red instead of reading as a clean registry.

src/features/overview/sub_events/libs/__tests__/eventSourceRegistry.test.ts:70 The absence assertion `uncovered` == [] at :74 carries a presence assertion on the needle population. The `#[cfg(test)]` tail cut was measured: every literal after the first cfg(test) in each file sits inside a test module today.
